deities: Swaminarayan (in the form of Hari Krishna)

history.period: Original temple built 1822-1824 by Swaminarayan; destroyed 26 January 2001; new temple inaugurated 15-23 May 2010
history.summary: The first temple of the Swaminarayan Sampraday, built in 1822-24 at Swaminarayan's own direction (land granted by Kutch ruler Rao Deshalji II) under the Nar Narayan Dev Gadi. The 2001 Bhuj earthquake destroyed the structure but the idols survived, and a new temple in marble and gold was built over five acres at a reported cost of about Rs 100 crore - 7 shikharas, 25 domes and 258 carved marble pillars, with the throne, domes and doors in gold. The original murtis (Nar Narayan, Hari Krishna, Radha Krishna, Ghanshyam, Sukh Shaiya) were reinstalled. CSV ERROR: the CSV 'state' column holds 'Bhuj', which is the town; the real state is Gujarat (district Kutch).

name: Swaminarayan Temple Bhuj
town_description: Bhuj is the historic walled capital of Kutch in western Gujarat, rebuilt after the devastating 26 January 2001 earthquake. It centres on Hamirsar Lake and is known for the Swaminarayan Mandir, Aina Mahal, Prag Mahal, the Kutch Museum and as the gateway to the Rann of Kutch.

travel.railway: Bhuj Railway Station, connected to Ahmedabad and Mumbai
travel.road: ~330 km from Ahmedabad by road; well connected to towns across Gujarat and Kutch

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Rann Utsav season (November-February) is popular.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Morning and evening aarti with darshan through the day; exact published timings unverified - confirm locally before visiting.
